exposure: Mode of delivery in the first pregnancy (total cesarean, emergency cesarean, planned cesarean, vaginal delivery)
Placental disease in the first pregnancy
outcome: Iatrogenic preterm delivery in the second pregnancy (<37 gestational weeks)
Spontaneous preterm delivery in the second pregnancy (<37 gestational weeks)
Placental disease in the second pregnancy
cohort: The study included 298,901 mothers with first and second singleton deliveries in Norway between 1999 and 2020.
finding: Compared with vaginal term delivery in the first pregnancy, cesarean delivery increases the risk of iatrogenic, but not spontaneous, preterm delivery in the subsequent pregnancy.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery in the first pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of iatrogenic preterm delivery in the second pregnancy, with a stronger association for previous planned cesarean delivery compared to emergency cesarean delivery.
gest_age: First pregnancies were at term; second pregnancy outcomes were preterm (<37 gestational weeks).
